This is the **merge step of a divide-and-conquer Voronoi/Delaunay construction** (Guibas–Stolfi style). The directory context (`voronoi_do_merge`) confirms it: it takes two already-built halves of the diagram and fuses them into one.

- **Quad-edge-like representation.** Node pointers are 128-byte-block addresses carrying a slot index (`p & 0x7f`). `p ^ 0x40` is the ""sym"" flip (opposite direction of the same edge), and following a link adds `0x20` to the slot (`(slot+0x20) & 0x7f`) — the classic `rot`/`onext` navigation. Each node holds a pointer to a point `{x, y, z}` (doubles at offsets 0/1/2).

- **Phase 1 — tangent search.** The two nested `while(true)` loops walk the left and right chains using only 2-D cross products on `(x, y)`, advancing one cursor while the other endpoint is ""inside"", flipping directions with `^ 0x40` — this locates the initial bridge (lower/upper tangent) between the two hulls.

- **Phase 2 — in-circle deletion + splicing.** The main loop tests candidate edges with a 4-point 3-D determinant (three cross-2-D terms weighted by the third coordinate `z`, the lifted coordinate, typically `x²+y²`) — this is exactly the **in-circle / empty-circle test** of Voronoi/Delaunay. Edges that fail are unlinked by swapping their encoded link fields with their neighbours (the paired `undefined8` exchanges = `splice`/`deleteEdge`) and pushed onto a **global free list** threaded through offset +8 of each block, headed by `DAT_00106088`. Valid frontier edges from the two halves are then joined by link swaps (`connect`), and both cursors advance.
